finding: The retained evidence manifest validates caller-supplied metadata but does not independently read retained artifact bytes. A manifest can therefore be internally well-formed while its declared SHA-256 digest or byte length no longer matches repository content.

verification.environment: isolated Node test runtime against byte-identical candidate source before commit

source_status.repository_observation: The existing retained-evidence-manifest implementation constructs its manifest from supplied path, sha256, and byte_length fields and does not read the referenced files.
source_status.primary_specification: FIPS 180-4 defines SHA-256 as a digest over the message bytes; integrity verification therefore requires recomputing the digest from the retained bytes rather than trusting a declared digest.
source_status.uncertainty: No authenticated end-to-end retained evidence capture was executed in this run. Runtime integration remains unverified.

falsification_route: Change any retained byte, declared digest, declared byte length, role, or evidence path and rerun the verifier. Downstream acceptance must fail before reconciliation or deployment assessment.
privacy_boundary: No credentials, private chat content, personal data, or raw provider payloads are retained in this artifact.
